questions.help:
Safe driving      
     
5 Driving in rain    
5.1 Adhesion - Grip
Always be cautious when the first drops of rain fall. Water mixed with dust, or other dirt from the road causes a layer of grease to be formed. This makes the road surface extremely slippery. When it rains heavier the road may be cleaned but this potentially may lead to further problems being caused, due to excess water on the road.
Motorcycle riders must pay special attention to road markings, as they may be very slippery.
(Página 228 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7.2 Windscreen wipers
However consideration must be given to the severity of the weather and the speed used must ensure that the visibility of the driver and ultimately safety is not compromised.
Windscreen wiper blades are an important safety element. For the windscreen to be cleaned properly the wiper blades must be in good condition. They should be regularly inspected, especially in preparation for winter.
The blades must be replaced, when they do not clean well (or leave marks), squeak or vibrate, symptoms that the rubber has hardened.
The windscreen wipers should not be used when the windscreen is dry as this may cause the windscreen to become smeared and further reduce visibility. It will also cause the glass to become scratched and lead to the wiper blades becoming damaged and wearing quicker.

Safe driving  
 
5 Driving in rain
5.1 Adhesion - Grip
In order to maintain the best possible adherence (grip) between your vehicle and the road surface – you should:
Maintain the tyres. This means the condition, (making sure there are no cuts, bulges, irregular tyre pattern etc.,) and the correct inflation pressure.
(Página 228 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Safe driving      
       
5 Driving in rain
5.1.1 Aquaplaning
Aquaplaning is caused by the accumulation of water on the road and by irregularities in its surface. Therefore, when it rains, it is necessary to pay special attention to potholes and areas in which puddles may occur.
This effect is more likely to occur with inappropriate speed and very wide or badly worn tyres.
One of the best solutions to avoid aquaplaning is to reduce the speed in the first instance, so that the tyres can displace the water and the wheels can retain contact with the road surface.
(Página 228 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Mechanics and maintenance
 
12 Wheels and tyres
12.1 Maintenance
It is necessary to periodically check that the rims do not show / display signs of oxidation or corrosion. Additionally, that there are no deformations or dents around the rim, caused by striking the pavement or other objects. It is also necessary to check the wheel bolts (nuts) are secure.
(Página 245 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Mechanics and maintenance
 
12 Wheels and tyres
12.1 Maintenance
Check the tyre pressures using a properly approved and tested tyre gauge at least once or twice a month. These can be found at public and private locations.
This is particularly important prior to commencing a journey where the vehicle will be travelling at high speed or where it will be heavily loaded. A tyre with badly adjusted pressure will wear unevenly as well as presenting an increased risk of a puncture or blow out. Fuel consumption is also increased.
(Página 245 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Mechanics and maintenance  
   
12 Wheels and tyres  
12.1 Maintenance
Periodically inspect the tyre. Check that the tread depth is above the tread wear indicators and verify that there are no foreign bodies in the tread (nails, stones, etc.) Also, check for irregular wear, cuts, cracks or deformation – if these are found the tyre may need to be replaced.
Consult a professional if abnormalities in the tyre(s) are found or the vehicle responds in an unexplained manner.
(Página 246 del manual 'Learning to drive')

ILLNESS AND MEDICATION  
 
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving
20.1 Respiratory allergies
Tips for drivers with allergies:
Not drive with the windows open. The air will contain large quantities of pollen, so it will increase the allergic reaction.
Do not put the air conditioning on strongly. The direct jets of air will cause an allergic reaction.
Keep the ventilation ducts clean. Clean the inside of the vehicle frequently, especially if animals are transported, and if possible fit special HEPA filters (high efficiency particulate air).
The holding capacity of the cabin air filter is limited. It is recommended to check it periodically, especially at the beginning of spring, replacing it if necessary.
(Página 47 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
2 Driver documentation      
     
2.2 The penalty point system    
Loss of points
Points are subtracted for each sanction that entails its loss. As a general rule, no more than eight points can be lost in a single day.
When drivers receive a non-appealable sanction in an administrative proceeding for committing any of the serious or very serious infractions that entail a loss of points, the points that are lost will be automatically and simultaneously deducted at the time when the violation is entered into the Registry of Drivers and Offenders. If one year has passed since the penalty became final and the related offence has not been recorded, the points will not be deducted.
A licence can be withdrawn as a consequence of losing all available points. It is then not possible to obtain a new licence for six months (three months for a professional driver).

questions.help:
11 Immobilisation ordered by the police
 
The agents of the authority in charge of traffic surveillance in the exercise of their job functions may proceed to immobilise the vehicle, as the result of the alleged infractions, when:
The driver refuses to take tests that are established for detecting possible intoxication by alcohol, narcotics, psychotropic drugs, stimulants and other analogous substances or the results of these tests are positive.
The vehicle does not have compulsory insurance.
Excess driving time or too few break times are observed, which are greater than 50 percent of the times established by regulation, except when the driver has been replaced (professional drivers).
There is excessive occupation of the vehicle, entailing increasing by 50 percent of the number of authorised occupants, excluding the driver.
A vehicle is being driven for which a permit of the type C or D is required, lacking the corresponding administrative authorization.
Drivers do not have the permit that authorises parking in zones with time restrictions or the authorised time is exceeded, until the driver is identified.
The immobilisation will be lifted in these cases at the time the reason leading to this action has ended.
(Página 200 del manual 'Learning to drive')

11 Immobilisation ordered by the police
 
11.1 Impounding a vehicle
The authority in charge of traffic management may proceed to removing the vehicle from the road using a tow truck and taking it to the appointed location in the following cases:
When a vehicle remains parked in lanes or parts of roads reserved exclusively for traffic or for the service of specific users or loading and unloading zones.
When a vehicle remains parked in locations enabled by the municipal authorities as parking with a time limit without placing the parking ticket that authorises parking or when passing triple the time paid pursuant to municipal ordinance.
When the vehicle blocks, makes difficult or entails a hazard for driving.
(Página 201 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Journeys and defensive and efficient driving          
           
DEFENSIVE DRIVING    
6 Maintaining space  
6.2 Stopping the vehicle
When stopping temporarily (for example, at a traffic light) it is necessary to maintain a frontal minimum distance of 2 or 3 metres from the vehicle ahead (As a guide you should be able to see the rear wheels of the car ahead of you touching the road.)
Maintaining an adequate gap ensures that;
If the vehicle in front rolls backwards the driver behind has ample time to warn the driver of this (prior to impact).
If the vehicle ahead stalls or breaks down the driver behind can manoeuvre around it.
If a vehicle is hit from behind it is provided with a sufficient gap to prevent it hitting the vehicle ahead.
(Página 274 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Transporting people and loads  
   
1 Generally
Therefore it is prohibited to travel with a mass (passengers or merchandise) above the maximum authorised mass of the vehicle.
Additionally, you cannot exceed the maximum authorised mass per axle or the maximum authorised mass of the set or combination.
It should be remembered that whatever the vehicle (or model), when it is loaded to the maximum limit, there will still be an effect on the handling and responses – for example an increase in the braking distance, reduction of acceleration, an increase in fuel consumption etc.
(Página 213 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Journeys and defensive and efficient driving             
           
1 Preparation for the trip      
1.3 Accessories, spare parts and tools      
Mixed vehicles and automobiles intended for goods transport (except for motor tricycles and heavy quadricycles) with an MAM no greater than 3,500 kg.
- The V-16 light-emitting hazard warning device or, failing this, two hazard warning triangles.
- A certified, high-visibility reflective vest inside the interior of the vehicle. It must be visible from at least 150 metres away. If the vehicle is an escort vehicle, protecting and accompanying others, vests must be worn by the driver and each member of the crew.
- A full-size spare or a temporary tyre, with the tools needed to change tyres, or an alternative system to changing them that offers sufficient guarantees for the mobility of the vehicle. In these cases, the vehicles will be driven in observance of the limitations of each alternative.
(Página 270 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Journeys and defensive and efficient driving         
       
1 Preparation for the trip    
1.3 Accessories, spare parts and tools    
Buses, as well as mixed vehicles and automobiles intended for goods transport, the latter two with a MMA exceeding 3,500 kg, and non-special sets of vehicles
- The V-16 light-emitting hazard warning device or, failing this, two hazard warning triangles.
- A certified, high-visibility reflective vest inside the interior of the vehicle. It must be visible from at least 150 metres away. If the vehicle is an escort vehicle, protecting and accompanying others, vests must be worn by the driver and each member of the crew.
- Homologated fire-extinction equipment that is suitable and in usage conditions.
(Página 270 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
¿En qué situaciones utilizará el alumbrado por el día?
In which situations will you use lights during the day?

answers.text:
Conduciendo una motocicleta o un ciclomotor solo cuando las condiciones meteorológicas disminuyan la visibilidad.
When riding a motorbike or moped only when visibility is reduced by the weather.

Las motocicletas y los vehículos que circulen por una vía con un carril en sentido contrario.
Motorbikes and vehicles travelling on a road with a lane where traffic travels in the opposite direction.

Cuando conduzca una motocicleta en cualquier tipo de vía y los vehículos que circulen por carriles habilitados en sentido contrario.
When riding a motorbike on any type of road and on vehicles travelling in a lane open to traffic travelling in the opposite direction.

questions.help:
8 Headlights - Low beam / dipped beam / short range  
   
8.2 Use of the low beam headlights
All motor vehicles and mopeds must use the low beam headlights (together with the position lights) when travelling:
Any hour of the day, when driving:
- On any lane of a road in which an additional circumstantial lane has been enabled.
- In a lane that has been enabled in a contrary direction to normal, that is, the use is exclusively reserved for certain users or due to exceptional circumstances, the direction for use has been changed.
- On the lane for the normal driving direction, adjacent to the one enabled for driving in the opposite direction than normal.
- In a reversible lane.
(Página 101 del manual 'Learning to drive')

8 Headlights - Low beam / dipped beam / short range    
     
8.2 Use of the low beam headlights
Motorbikes travelling on any road during on the day must use dipped headlights, unless they have their daytime running lights on, provided the visibility conditions are suitable.
(Página 102 del manual 'Learning to drive')
